finding.claim: Unauthenticated /preview fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL with no validation and returns the status code and the first 500 characters of the body. This is full-read SSRF. It can reach internal services, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) and localhost.
finding.source: request.args.get('url') in preview(), the ?url= query parameter
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5), with the response body returned in the JSON

trace.note: requests.get(target) is called directly; redirects are followed by default and any scheme, host or IP is accepted
resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: None. No scheme check, host allow-list, private-IP block, or redirect restriction on this path.

verdict.reason: app.py:15-17 takes the url query parameter and passes it straight to requests.get at line 16, then returns the status code and the first 500 characters of the body; the route has no auth, no before_request hooks and no host or scheme check (the ALLOWED_HOSTS check at line 24 applies only to /partner).

finding.claim: The /partner allow-list check is bypassable. It validates only the hostname parsed by urlparse. The request is then sent by requests (urllib3) with allow_redirects left at its default of True. If any allow-listed host has an open redirect, or if the two parsers disagree on a crafted URL, the request reaches an arbitrary host. Only the status code is returned, so this is blind SSRF. The redirect route depends on an allow-listed host exposing an open redirect, which I could not verify from this code.
finding.source: request.args.get('url') in partner(), the ?url= query parameter

trace.note: host = urlparse(target).hostname is parsed with urllib.parse
Check: host must be in ALLOWED_HOSTS
requests.get(target) re-parses the raw string with a different parser and follows redirects, so the check on the first hop does not cover later hops

finding.guards_checked: Hostname allow-list on the urlparse result only. There is no scheme restriction, no allow_redirects=False, no pinning of the parsed URL, and no IP check. Matches the pattern in case 04 (url-validate-reparse).

verdict.guard_found: Exact set membership of urlparse(target).hostname in ALLOWED_HOSTS (app.py:23-25); no allow_redirects=False or scheme check.
verdict.reason: The trace matches app.py:22-26 and the source is attacker-controlled. However, app.py:24 is an exact hostname set-membership guard, so exploitation depends on an allow-listed host exposing an open redirect (or a urlparse/urllib3 parser differential), and neither can be determined from this code.
